messages:
emma (Support): heads up — customer `acme-inc` reports missing audit events for 2024-03-10..2024-03-12. their SIEM shows repeated 403 on the export endpoint. can eng-sec triage?

mike (Eng-Sec): thx. any request IDs or sample manifests? 403 usually KMS or ACL.

emma (Support): pasted snippets from the tenant's forwarder logs below: 
```
2024-03-11T09:14:02Z ERROR forwarder.Upload failed status=403 keyId=arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456:key/abcd-1234 ctx="Encrypt failed: AccessDeniedException"
2024-03-11T09:14:02Z WARN forwarder.Retrying attempt=1
```

sasha (SRE): also seeing spikes in 429s around that window. could be burst policy + auth expiry. did they recently rotate KMS alias or remove a cross-account grant?

rahul (Infra): checking KMS key rotation logs and grants now. possible race if rekey job ran 2024-03-11T09:10Z. will pull CloudTrail for Decrypt/Encrypt calls.

emma (Support): customer says they rotated their key the morning of 3/11. they tried replaying manifests; SIEM still rejects payloads with 403.

mike (Eng-Sec): if the key was re-created (new key ID) but forwarder still targets old alias+grant, decrypt will fail. two quick repro asks: 1) can support share the exact s3 manifest & object path that failed? 2) forwarder config (kms_key_alias or key_id) and IAM role ARN.

emma (Support): sending manifest link to private thread (redacted here). forwarding `forwarder.conf` snippet they used: 
```
output_s3_bucket = "acme-audit-exports"
kms_key_alias = "alias/acme-audit-key"
role_arn = "arn:aws:iam::999999:role/forwarder-role"
```

sasha (SRE): ask customer to run quick check: `aws kms list-grants --key-id alias/acme-audit-key` and `aws kms describe-key --key-id alias/acme-audit-key`. if list-grants returns none for forwarder-role, that's the reason. also check forwarder clock drift; signatures expire.

mike (Eng-Sec): adding an internal mitigator: can we support a short-lived fallback to a service-managed re-encrypt path so their SIEM can backfill without exposing keys? if not immediate, document replay steps.

rahul (Infra): preliminary CloudTrail shows a DeleteGrant + CreateGrant sequence at 2024-03-11T09:09:56Z for that key. grantId changed. that aligns with failures at 09:14. looks like the forwarder had grant reference to the old grant id.

emma (Support): customer asking for repro steps so they can unblock their SOC. they want exact CLI commands to replay safely.

mike (Eng-Sec): recommended replay plan (short):
1) confirm forwarder has a grant for the current KMS key and role: `aws kms list-grants --key-id <key> | grep <forwarder-role>`
2) if missing, create grant: `aws kms create-grant --key-id <key> --grantee-principal <role_arn> --operations Encrypt Decrypt`
3) trigger forwarder to reprocess failed manifest: `POST /v1/admin/forwarder/reprocess { "manifest_path": "s3://..." }` (support can proxy if customer can't hit admin endpoint)
4) monitor forwarder logs for successful `Encrypt` and S3 put status=200.

sasha (SRE): +check for rate limits: bump `concurrency_limit` temporarily during replay to avoid 429s. also watch for token TTLs if forwarder uses STS.

emma (Support): relayed plan to customer. they asked whether any exports were permanently lost during the rotation window.

mike (Eng-Sec): unlikely lost — objects that failed to upload should still exist as local forwarder pending payloads or in dead-letter queue. ask for forwarder `pending/` directory listing. if objects are gone, we'll need S3 server logs to trace PUT attempts.

forwarder-bot: automated-alert: forwarder-v2 deployed to prod 2024-02-28 (no changes to kms handling).

rahul (Infra): will follow up with CloudTrail evidence and a short write-up for the customer about safe key rotation patterns (create new grant before deleting old one).

emma (Support): thanks all — customer on call at 1600PT. i'll ping when they confirm replay succeeded or if they need us to run the `create-grant` step for them. :thumbsup:
